page.layout: One page of text in a single column; the left edge of the scan is cut off, so many lines begin with fragments. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Catchword at the foot right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: efte Nonio Marcello peripatetico, cap. 6. ubi inquit fervere non solùm est ex in-cendio calere, sed ex quibuscunque mo-lestiis perturbari, unde & æstus marini & exæstuatio animi sub hac significatio-ne recte posita sentiuntur, hinc Virgilius Georg. l. I.
main_text.head: Fervere.
main_text.p: Nec dispari sensu Plinius, lib. 17. cap. 2. Tellus, inquit, nive fermen-tescit: & Galenus, terram fermentari atra bile quae acore suo eam solvit, docet lib. de atra bile: nam & fermentum dici à ferveo, neminem, uti opinor, fugit. Sed quid multis? res ipsa loqua-tur, Sal Tartari & Spiritus Vitrioli, aut spiritus salis, acetum & creta, ce-revisia pocularis, & infinita alia frigi-dâ effervescentiâ ebulliunt; frigida, inquam, respectu aëris in quo illa ctio exercetur, uti si vitreo tubulo, in cum finem excogitato à Doctore

page.notes: The left edge of the scan is cut, so the first letters of several lines are missing and are given as printed fragments (efte, ur, aut, ctio, cum, ebulliunt lines). Words such as "tensu" and the Latin passage at the foot are read as printed; the verse lines in italic are not marked as separate verse elements. The catchword "Swam-" is the start of the next page's first word.
